title: The Person of Christ
summary: Who Jesus is: the eternal Son of God, born of a virgin, truly God and truly man in one Person.
description: This course studies the doctrine of Christ's Person. It shows from Scripture that Jesus is the eternal Son of God, that He became truly human through the virgin birth, that He is one Person with two natures, and that He was sinless. It explains how the early church guarded these truths at Chalcedon, and considers His offices as Prophet, Priest and King and His present exaltation.
objectives: Show the eternal existence and full deity of the Son
Explain the incarnation and the virgin birth
Show Christ's true and complete humanity
Explain the union of two natures in one Person and the errors it excludes
outcomes: Give Bible evidence for Christ's pre-existence and deity
Explain why the virgin birth matters
Show evidence of Jesus' human body, mind and emotions
State the Chalcedonian definition in simple words

modules.title: The Eternal Son
modules.intro: Jesus did not begin at Bethlehem. This week we see that the Son existed eternally with the Father.

lessons.title: Before Abraham was, I am
lessons.body:
The Son existed before His human birth. "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God" (John 1:1). Jesus prayed for "the glory which I had with thee before the world was" (John 17:5) and said, "Before Abraham was, I am" (John 8:58), using God's own name (Exodus 3:14). His hearers understood and took up stones.

Micah prophesied that the ruler born in Bethlehem had goings forth "from of old, from everlasting" (Micah 5:2).

The Son is not a created being; He is the eternal Creator.

lessons.title: He thought it not robbery
lessons.body:
Philippians 2:6-8 is a great hymn about Christ. "Being in the form of God", He "thought it not robbery to be equal with God: But made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant".

He did not stop being God; He added humanity and laid aside the outward display of His glory and privileges, humbling Himself even to the death of the cross.

Therefore God highly exalted Him, so that "every knee should bow" and every tongue confess "that Jesus Christ is Lord" (2:9-11), echoing words Isaiah used of the LORD Himself (Isaiah 45:23).

lessons.title: Jesus' divine claims and works
lessons.body:
Jesus claimed and did what belongs to God alone:

- He forgave sins against God (Mark 2:5-7).
- He accepted worship (John 9:38; 20:28).
- He claimed oneness with the Father: "I and my Father are one" (John 10:30).
- He said He would judge all people (Matthew 25:31-32).
- He controlled nature, raised the dead and rose Himself (John 11:43-44).

C. S. Lewis famously noted that such claims leave three options: liar, lunatic, or Lord. His life, teaching and resurrection show He is Lord (Romans 1:4).

terms.def: Christ's existence as the eternal Son before His human birth.
The truth that Jesus is fully God.
God's covenant name, claimed by Jesus in John 8:58.
Christ's true divine nature, which He possessed before the incarnation.
The true humanity and lowly state Christ took for our salvation.
The title of divine authority confessed of Jesus.

texts.teaches: The Word was in the beginning with God and was God.
Jesus said, 'Before Abraham was, I am.'
Christ, being in the form of God, was equal with God.
Only God can forgive sins, yet Jesus forgave sins.
Christ was declared the Son of God with power by the resurrection.

He humbled Himself, adding humanity without ceasing to be God.
He claimed and did what only God does.
His resurrection declares Him the Son of God with power.

modules.title: The Word Made Flesh
modules.intro: The eternal Son became man. This week we study the incarnation and the virgin birth.

lessons.title: The incarnation
lessons.body:
"And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us" (John 1:14). The **incarnation** means the eternal Son took to Himself a real human nature, body and soul, without ceasing to be God.

He "was made in the likeness of men" (Philippians 2:7), "made of a woman, made under the law" (Galatians 4:4).

Why? To reveal the Father (John 1:18), to be our substitute and High Priest, sharing our flesh and blood so He could die for us (Hebrews 2:14-17), and to be our example (1 Peter 2:21). Only one who is both God and man can bring God and man together.

lessons.title: Born of a virgin
lessons.body:
Isaiah prophesied, "a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel" (Isaiah 7:14), fulfilled in Jesus (Matthew 1:22-23).

Matthew and Luke both record that Mary conceived by the Holy Ghost before she and Joseph came together (Matthew 1:18-25; Luke 1:34-35). The angel said, "that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God" (Luke 1:35).

The virgin birth is a miracle, not a myth. All Bible-believing churches, including Baptist and Deeper Life, confess it as essential.

lessons.title: Why the virgin birth matters
lessons.body:
The virgin birth shows that salvation comes from God, not human effort; the Saviour came by God's initiative.

It shows how Jesus could be both God and man: conceived by the Holy Ghost, born of a woman.

It is connected with His sinlessness. Though truly human, He did not inherit Adam's guilt and corruption; He was "holy, harmless, undefiled, separate from sinners" (Hebrews 7:26). The Spirit's work in His conception kept Him holy (Luke 1:35).

To deny the virgin birth is to doubt both Scripture's truth and God's power.

terms.def: The eternal Son of God taking a true human nature.

'God with us', the name given in Isaiah 7:14.

A virgin shall conceive and bear a son named Immanuel.

He became man to reveal God, die as our substitute and be our High Priest.
He was conceived by the Holy Ghost and born of the virgin Mary.
The virgin birth shows God's initiative and is linked to Christ's sinlessness.

modules.title: Truly Man
modules.intro: Jesus is not God pretending to be human. This week we see His true humanity and His sinlessness.

lessons.title: A real human body and mind
lessons.body:
Jesus had a real body: He was born, grew (Luke 2:52), was hungry (Matthew 4:2), thirsty (John 19:28) and tired (John 4:6). He slept in a boat (Mark 4:38), bled and died.

He had a real human mind: He "increased in wisdom and stature" (Luke 2:52) and asked questions.

He had real emotions: He wept at Lazarus's tomb (John 11:35), was angry at hardness of heart (Mark 3:5), rejoiced in the Spirit (Luke 10:21), and was "exceeding sorrowful, even unto death" in Gethsemane (Matthew 26:38).

lessons.title: Tempted, yet without sin
lessons.body:
Jesus was truly tempted. He was led into the wilderness "to be tempted of the devil" (Matthew 4:1), and Hebrews says He "was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin" (Hebrews 4:15).

He never sinned. He challenged His enemies, "Which of you convinceth me of sin?" (John 8:46). Peter: He "did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth" (1 Peter 2:22). Paul: He "knew no sin" (2 Corinthians 5:21).

Because He felt the full force of temptation and never gave in, He can help us when we are tempted (Hebrews 2:18).

lessons.title: Why His humanity matters
lessons.body:
Christ's humanity is not a lesser truth. If He were not truly man:

- He could not be our **substitute**, dying in human nature for human sin (Hebrews 2:17).
- He could not be our **mediator**: "one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus" (1 Timothy 2:5).
- He could not be our **example** of obedience and faith (1 Peter 2:21).
- He could not be our **sympathetic High Priest** (Hebrews 4:15-16).

John warns that denying "that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh" is the spirit of antichrist (1 John 4:2-3). He is still a man, glorified, today.

terms.def: The truth that Jesus is fully and truly human.
The teaching that Christ not only did not sin but could not sin.
Christ's perfect freedom from all sin.
One who stands between two parties to reconcile them; Christ between God and man.
The early error that Christ only seemed to have a human body.
Christ, who feels our weakness because He was tempted as we are.

Jesus wept.
Christ was tempted in all points like us, yet without sin.
Christ knew no sin, yet was made sin for us.
There is one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus.

summary: Jesus had a real human body, mind and emotions.
He was truly tempted but never sinned.
His humanity makes Him our substitute, mediator, example and sympathetic priest.
Denying Christ came in the flesh is the spirit of antichrist.

modules.title: One Person, Two Natures
modules.intro: How can Jesus be both God and man? This week we study the union of two natures in one Person and the errors the church rejected.

lessons.title: The hypostatic union
lessons.body:
Jesus is one Person with two natures, divine and human, united without being mixed. Theologians call this the **hypostatic union** (from the Greek for "person").

This explains why Scripture says things of Christ that belong to one nature or the other: He is eternal (as God) and was born (as man); He knows all things (John 21:17) and did not know the day of His return (Mark 13:32); He upholds all things (Hebrews 1:3) and slept in a boat.

Yet it is always the one Person, the Son, who does and suffers all these things. "God... purchased [the church] with his own blood" (Acts 20:28).

lessons.title: Errors the church rejected
lessons.body:
- **Ebionism:** Jesus was only a man, specially blessed.
- **Docetism and Gnosticism:** Jesus only seemed to be human.
- **Arianism:** the Son is a created being.
- **Apollinarianism:** Jesus had a human body but a divine mind instead of a human mind.
- **Nestorianism:** Christ was two persons, a man and God joined together.
- **Eutychianism:** the two natures mixed into a third, neither fully God nor fully man.

Each error weakens either His deity, His humanity, or the unity of His Person, and so weakens the gospel.

lessons.title: The Chalcedonian definition
lessons.body:
In AD 451 the Council of Chalcedon summed up the biblical teaching: Christ is "truly God and truly man", "of one substance with the Father" as to His deity and "of one substance with us" as to His humanity, "in two natures, without confusion, without change, without division, without separation".

These four "withouts" guard the truth: the natures are not mixed or changed (against Eutychianism), and not divided or separated (against Nestorianism).

Chalcedon does not explain the mystery fully, but it sets a fence around it. Baptist, Pentecostal and Holiness churches all confess this faith.

terms.def: The union of Christ's divine and human natures in one Person.
The error of dividing Christ into two persons.
The error of mixing Christ's natures into one new nature.

Scripture speaks of Him according to each nature, but always as one Person.

modules.title: Prophet, Priest and King
modules.intro: Christ fulfils the three great offices of the Old Testament. This week we see His work as Prophet, Priest and King, and His present exaltation.

lessons.title: Prophet
lessons.body:
Moses promised that God would raise up "a Prophet... like unto me" (Deuteronomy 18:15). Peter applies this to Jesus (Acts 3:22-23).

Christ is more than a prophet; He is the Word Himself. God "hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son" (Hebrews 1:2). He revealed the Father (John 1:18) and taught with authority (Matthew 7:29).

He continues His prophetic work through His Word and Spirit. The Father says, "This is my beloved Son... hear ye him" (Matthew 17:5).

lessons.title: Priest
lessons.body:
A priest represents people before God, offers sacrifice and intercedes. Christ is "a great high priest, that is passed into the heavens" (Hebrews 4:14), "after the order of Melchisedec" (Hebrews 7:17), not of Levi.

Unlike earthly priests, He offered Himself, once for all: "by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption" (Hebrews 9:12).

He now "ever liveth to make intercession" for those who come to God by Him (Hebrews 7:25). We need no other priest or mediator to approach God.

lessons.title: King
lessons.body:
Christ is the promised Son of David whose kingdom has no end (Luke 1:32-33). He was born King of the Jews, entered Jerusalem as King, and was crucified under the title "KING OF THE JEWS" (Matthew 27:37).

Raised and ascended, He sits at the Father's right hand, "far above all principality, and power" (Ephesians 1:20-22). "All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth" (Matthew 28:18).

He reigns now over His church and over all things, and He will return as "KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS" (Revelation 19:16). Our response is to bow to Him as Lord.

terms.def: Christ's work as Prophet, Priest and King.
One who speaks God's word; Christ is God's final Word.
One who offers sacrifice and intercedes; Christ offered Himself and intercedes.
One who rules; Christ reigns over all things.
The priest-king of Salem whose order Christ's priesthood follows.

summary: As Prophet, Christ is God's final Word.
As Priest, He offered Himself once for all and intercedes for us.
As King, He reigns now and will return in glory.
We hear Him, trust Him and obey Him.

short.q: Give two Bible evidences of Christ's pre-existence.

short.q: Why does the virgin birth matter?
short.model: It shows salvation comes from God's initiative, explains how Jesus is both God and man, and is linked to His sinlessness.

short.q: Give three evidences of Jesus' true humanity.
short.model: He was born and grew, was hungry, thirsty and tired; He wept and felt sorrow; He increased in wisdom and was tempted.

short.q: Why must Christ be both God and man to save us?
short.model: As man He could die as our substitute; as God His sacrifice has infinite worth; as both He is the mediator who reconciles God and man.

short.q: State the Chalcedonian definition in simple words.
short.model: Christ is one Person in two natures, truly God and truly man, without the natures being mixed, changed, divided or separated.
He offered Himself once for all as the perfect sacrifice, and now intercedes for His people at God's right hand.
